summary:
### Project Overview

SpaceAnalog Explorer is an interactive platform designed to identify Earth locations that have environmental characteristics similar to selected regions on the Moon and Mars. The project aims to help researchers explore Earth-based analog environments that can support future space exploration.

### How Does It Work?

The platform compares environmental factors such as temperature, elevation, slope, surface roughness, and dryness between selected Earth locations and Moon or Mars regions. It uses data processing and a similarity-scoring approach to rank Earth locations according to how closely their environmental characteristics match the selected planetary region.

### Technologies Used

We plan to use Python for programming, Streamlit for developing the interactive website, Pandas and NumPy for data processing, Scikit-learn for similarity analysis, Plotly for interactive visualizations, and Folium for interactive maps. We aim to use relevant NASA datasets for Earth, Moon, and Mars environmental information.

### Benefits and Intended Impact

This project can help users explore potential Earth analog environments for studying extreme conditions and preparing technologies for future lunar and Martian missions. It provides an accessible way to compare planetary environments through maps, graphs, anore different planetary regions, compare environmental characteristics, and identify possible Earth analog locations in an understandable visual format.
